title: Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online

reading.body:
An AI image generation system was used to create non-consensual sexual imagery of a real person without her knowledge or consent. The person deploying the system obtained source photographs from the victim's social media accounts and then used AI to generate explicit images morphed to her likeness. No content moderation or output review appears to have prevented distribution of the material across multiple platforms and accounts.

The deployment failure was human rather than technical. The system itself lacked the safeguards to detect and refuse requests for non-consensual sexual imagery, or lacked enforcement of such safeguards. No human reviewer checked the output before it was distributed. The person using the system deliberately obscured his identity across multiple platforms and accounts, suggesting awareness that the conduct was wrong.

It is not established whether the AI system had safety features designed to prevent this use, whether they failed, or what technical measures might have stopped distribution once the images were created.

reports.title: Delhi: Man held for circulating obscene AI-generated photos of college acquaintance
Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online

summary:
A 22-year-old man named Keshav Bansal was arrested in Delhi for creating and spreading sexually explicit artificial intelligence-generated images of a college acquaintance. He obtained photographs from the woman's private social media accounts and used AI technology to create obscene morphed images. Bansal operated multiple fake accounts on Instagram, Discord, and Facebook using different email addresses to hide his identity while distributing the harmful content and sending threatening messages to the victim.

The woman filed a complaint with the Cyber Police Station in North Delhi after receiving messages from anonymous accounts informing her that her morphed photographs were being circulated on Discord servers. Police investigated the digital evidence and traced the fake profiles back to Bansal. During questioning, he admitted knowing the complainant from college and said personal resentment had developed between them. Police recovered his mobile phone, SIM cards, and other digital evidence, with the investigation continuing.
